clue.text: Nervous — and imperfect, perhaps?

definitions.meaning: nervous means on edge, strung up
the imperfect is one example of a verb form expressing time in grammar, like the past or future

explanation.surface: Someone anxious and flawed, perhaps.
explanation.definitionFit: Edgy people are strained and taut; the imperfect is a grammatical category of time for verbs, hence 'perhaps'.

clue.text: Change coaches with one leaving behind time

indicators.note: leaving says the numeral departs from the word for coaches

parts.note: coaches are railway carriages, making up trains
I is the Roman numeral one
behind time means late

explanation.surface: Swapping coaches, with one departing late.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one leaving' takes I out of TRAINS, giving TRANS.
explanation.definitionFit: To render something into another language is to alter its form while keeping its meaning.

clue.text: Geordie mate gets a place in the mountains …

parts.note: a Geordie comes from Newcastle in the North East of England, abbreviated NE
a mate is a friend, a pal

explanation.surface: A Newcastle man's friend takes a mountain trip.
explanation.walkthrough: A Geordie is a native of Newcastle upon Tyne in north-east England.
explanation.definitionFit: The Himalayan kingdom contains Everest and many of the world's highest peaks.

clue.text: .. Edward providing glacial material for building?

parts.note: Ed is a short form of Edward
providing means if, on condition that
glaciers are made of ice

explanation.surface: Edward supplies glacier stuff for a construction project.
explanation.definitionFit: An imposing structure such as a large edifice is a grand building.

clue.text: Harassed press for introducing old don?

indicators.note: introducing says one piece is brought inside the other
harassed suggests being harried and knocked about, so the letters of press for are jumbled

explanation.surface: A newspaper pressured into presenting some elderly academic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Harassed' rearranges PRESS FOR into PROFESSR, and 'introducing' puts O inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A don is a university teacher, especially at Oxford or Cambridge, and a senior one holds a chair.

clue.text: Write about a male water bird

indicators.note: about says the writing word goes round the other pieces

parts.note: to pen is to write
he is the male pronoun

explanation.surface: Composing something on a male duck or swan.
explanation.walkthrough: The word 'water' does no work in the wordplay; it rides on the fact that a female swan, also a writing implement's name, is a water bird. Peafowl are not water birds.
explanation.definitionFit: The female of the peafowl is the drab partner of the peacock.

clue.text: 'Accio Pint!' cooked up, with one about to leave person doling out glasses

indicators.note: cooked up says the remaining letters are concocted into a new order
to leave says that abbreviation drops out of the fodder

parts.note: C, short for circa, means about

explanation.surface: A Harry Potter-style summoning spell for a pint, then a barman serving drinks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Accio' is the summoning charm in Harry Potter. One C is removed from ACCIOPINT and the rest rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who dispenses spectacles is an eye-care professional, the glasses here being lenses rather than drinks.

clue.text: Absolute ruler in temper, originally

indicators.note: in says the answer sits inside the following words

explanation.surface: A despot who started out with a temper.
explanation.definitionFit: A supreme monarch reigning over an empire wields total power.

clue.text: Observer's a weekly publication

definitions.meaning: A long-running British weekly current affairs magazine

explanation.surface: The Observer newspaper described as a weekly paper.
explanation.walkthrough: The Observer is a British Sunday paper, hence the misdirection; the weekly is The Spectator, a British political magazine.
explanation.definitionFit: An onlooker watching a match is a watcher, and the magazine bears the same name.

clue.text: It can locate things in the dark or fog, either way

definitions.text: It can locate things in the dark or fog
definitions.note: the whole description is the definition, and the word it describes is a palindrome, so it reads the same either way

indicators.note: either way says the word reads the same forwards and backwards

parts.words: It can locate things in the dark or fog
parts.note: the whole description is the definition, and the word it describes is a palindrome, so it reads the same either way

explanation.surface: A device that finds objects in poor visibility.
explanation.definitionFit: This detection system bounces radio waves off objects, finding them unseen.

clue.text: Pal can tip off one looking for a job

indicators.note: off suggests something gone wrong or out of order, so the letters of pal can tip are rearranged

explanation.surface: A friend may tip off a jobseeker about a vacancy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tip off' reads as a phrase meaning 'warn', but 'tip' is fodder and 'off' the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who applies for a post is a candidate seeking work.

clue.text: Beg to go first after parking

indicators.note: after places the piece for going first behind the parking letter

parts.note: P is the road-sign abbreviation for parking
to go first is to lead

explanation.surface: A plea to be allowed to drive off first once parked.
explanation.definitionFit: To beg is to implore earnestly, as a defendant or supplicant does.

clue.text: Flag displayed next to short girl — a flag!

indicators.note: next to says the two pieces sit side by side

parts.note: Sal is a short form of the girl's name Sally
to flag is to tire, to lose energy

explanation.surface: A banner shown beside a little girl, and it's a banner too.
explanation.walkthrough: The first 'Flag' is a verb meaning to weaken; only the last words define. A saltire is the X-shaped cross of St Andrew on Scotland's flag.
explanation.definitionFit: A saltire is a diagonal-cross banner, most famously Scotland's national emblem.

clue.text: Show organiser putting scoundrel on a high spot

indicators.note: on says the scoundrel piece is placed before the rest in an across answer

parts.note: a cur is a contemptible man
a tor is a rocky hill, especially on Dartmoor

explanation.surface: Someone staging an exhibition by putting a villain up on a hilltop.
explanation.definitionFit: A museum or gallery keeper arranges exhibitions, so organises shows.

clue.text: This should be the very solution that you enter

definitions.text: This should be the very solution that you enter

parts.words: This should be the very solution that you enter
parts.note: the clue describes itself: what goes into this light is simply the reply to any clue

explanation.definitionFit: A reply to a question or puzzle is exactly what a solver writes into the grid.

clue.text: Pulled out of contest that's marked

definitions.meaning: a horse withdrawn from a race is struck off the list
marked means bearing scrapes or scores on its surface

explanation.surface: A competitor withdrawn because they were scarred.
explanation.definitionFit: Withdrawn runners are deleted from the card; a scuffed surface bears scrapes.

clue.text: Went quickly back, made an assessment and told a story

indicators.note: back says the word for went quickly is read in the opposite direction

parts.note: went quickly means ran
to make an assessment of something is to rate it

explanation.surface: Someone rushed back, gave a verdict and recounted it all.
explanation.definitionFit: To recount a tale is to relate it, the storyteller's work.

clue.text: 24-hour hallucinations or hopeful aspirations?

parts.note: a day lasts 24 hours
dreams are visions, imaginings

explanation.surface: Visions lasting all day, or just wishful hopes.
explanation.definitionFit: Idle reveries about what one wishes would happen are wistful fantasies.

clue.text: Something to savour: the setter attending a dance

parts.note: the setter refers to themself as me
attending an event is being at it
a ball is a formal dance

explanation.surface: A crossword compiler enjoying a dance.
explanation.definitionFit: A savoury rissole of minced beef is a tasty morsel; 'savour' hints at savoury food.

clue.text: Inhabitants of planet getting listening device, then trapping leader of Martians

parts.note: the ear is the organ of hearing

indicators.note: trapping says one piece holds another inside it
leader of picks the opening letter of Martians

explanation.surface: Sci-fi: planet dwellers acquire a listening device and then capture the Martian chief.
explanation.walkthrough: 'then' gives itself, THEN, which traps the M.
explanation.definitionFit: People of our own world, as science fiction calls those who live on the third planet.

clue.text: Large-scale place to live, needing half of great wealth

parts.note: a home is a dwelling

indicators.note: half of keeps the first three of six letters of the word for great wealth

parts.note: riches means great wealth

explanation.surface: A house that needs only half a fortune.
explanation.definitionFit: Epic in scale, like Homer's Iliad and Odyssey, so vast and heroic.

clue.text: Slick sergeant-major facing soldiers

indicators.note: facing puts the abbreviation for the sergeant-major in front of the troops

parts.note: soldiers collectively form an army

explanation.surface: An oily NCO addressing his troops on parade.
explanation.definitionFit: Slick here means oily and ingratiating, unctuously charming.

clue.text: Second Reagan in charge? That's stupid

parts.note: a mo is a moment, a second
Ronald Reagan, US president, is Ron for short

explanation.surface: Mocking the idea of Reagan taking command for a second term.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiotic behaviour is foolish, lacking sense or intelligence.

clue.text: Much too theatrical: buck up you old …

parts.note: a buck is a male deer, a stag

indicators.note: up in a down answer says the old pronoun is read bottom to top

parts.note: ye is the old form of you

explanation.surface: An exhortation to cheer up an old ham actor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'buck up' looks like a phrase meaning cheer up, but buck is the deer and 'up' reverses YE to EY.
explanation.definitionFit: Overacted, affected behaviour is exaggerated, as if performed on a stage.

clue.text: City that's dull — it may get wet after a shower

definitions.text: it may get wet after a shower

parts.note: Bath is a city in Somerset, England
matt or mat describes a dull, unglossy finish

explanation.surface: A dreary town where it rains a lot.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests rain on a city; the shower is the bathroom kind.
explanation.definitionFit: A small floor rug by the tub soaks up drips when someone steps out after washing.

clue.text: .. dim, initially boring, Shakespearean character

indicators.note: initially picks the first letter of boring

parts.note: King Lear is the title character of a Shakespeare tragedy

explanation.surface: A dull, tedious figure from Shakespeare.
explanation.definitionFit: Bleary or blurred vision is clouded, unclear.

clue.text: Dog that's more like Terence?

definitions.meaning: a small dog bred for hunting burrowing animals
Terence is often shortened to Terry, so someone more like a Terry is jokingly more Terry-ish

explanation.surface: Is this dog more like someone called Terence?
explanation.walkthrough: A whimsical comparative built on Terry, the usual nickname for Terence.
explanation.definitionFit: An earth dog such as a Jack Russell or Yorkie belongs to this breed group.

clue.text: You could see this on a cake in the freezer?

definitions.text: You could see this on a cake
definitions.meaning: sugar coating spread on top of a cake
something in the freezer is freezing, turning to ice

explanation.surface: A cake in the freezer might have frost on it.
explanation.definitionFit: A sweet topping covers cakes, and the word also means becoming frozen.

clue.text: A number rule the roost, to some extent

indicators.note: to some extent says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A digit that dominates, partially.
explanation.walkthrough: 'number' is read as something that numbs, not a figure.
explanation.definitionFit: This volatile liquid was an early anaesthetic, so it deadens feeling, a numbing agent.

clue.text: Tangier confused North American: it's in South America

indicators.note: confused says the letters of Tangier are mixed up

explanation.surface: A North American traveller muddles Morocco with a South American country.
explanation.definitionFit: The country in question lies in the southern cone of that continent.

clue.text: Essentially sharp about appearing in motoring event

indicators.note: appearing in says the turned piece goes inside the motoring event

parts.note: a rally is a motoring competition on public roads

indicators.note: about says the word for sharp is turned round

parts.note: acid means sharp, tart

explanation.surface: A keen remark about showing up at a car rally.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sharp' looks like a modifier of the definition but is the tart-tasting synonym, turned round by 'about'.
explanation.definitionFit: Radically means at the root, fundamentally, in essence.

clue.text: Conservative given a long time in prisons

parts.note: ages means a long time

explanation.surface: A Tory politician sentenced to a long stretch inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Enclosures with bars confine animals or people, so they serve as jails.
